html:
The Mdewakanton, "people of Spirit Lake", are one of the four bands of the Santee or Eastern Dakota, part of the people often called the Sioux. Their old home was Mille Lacs Lake in central Minnesota. With the Wahpekute they formed the Upper Council of the Santee.

In the mid 1700s wars with the Ojibwe pushed them south from Mille Lacs to the Mississippi and Minnesota rivers, near today's Twin Cities. In treaties of 1851 they sold most of their land to the United States for a narrow reservation and annual payments. When the payments failed and families went hungry, the Mdewakanton leader Little Crow led the Dakota War of 1862. After it, the army hanged 38 Dakota men at Mankato, the largest mass execution in American history, and the Dakota were expelled from Minnesota. Some families later returned, and their descendants live in small Dakota communities in Minnesota today.
